summary: Cazadero volunteers built a lookout on Red Oat Mountain in 1967; it moved to Pole Mountain in 1981, and a steel replacement was in final construction in late 2024.

facts.design: Two-story wooden tower (moved 1981); replacement building built mainly of steel

access.note: Preserve hiking is open to the public. The lookout is not a walk-in visit; general visits are arranged through CAL Fire or the association.

visit.trail_note: Hike in from the Jenner Headlands parking lot on Highway 1; the summit route is a 15-mile roundtrip.

events.note: Built by Cazadero residents on Red Oat Mountain, not at the current site.
Moved from Red Oat Mountain to Pole Mountain.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on June 4, 1998.
Sonoma Land Trust closed escrow on the 238-acre Pole Mountain Preserve after the Elliott family decided to sell.
Old wooden tower taken out of service after years of wear, per the 2019 Press Democrat. The 2018 volunteer report says staffing ran until 2018.
Volunteer report says the tower was staffed every year for 35 years, until 2018. Conflicts with the 2017 closure date.
A newly installed 360-degree camera was photographed on the tower on Aug. 7, 2019.
An effort to raise an initial $100,000 for a new steel tower was under way in 2019 (Press Democrat).
Land trust newsletter says the old tower had become too unsafe to staff.
Group posted that construction of the new lookout station had begun (April 9, 2024).
Group said in November 2024 that the new steel building was in its final stages of construction. Opening was not confirmed in the pages read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2019 Press Democrat article says the wooden tower was taken out of service in 2017, while a 2018 volunteer report says it was staffed until 2018. The story reports both and leaves the closing date disputed.
The land trust gives the summit as 2,204 ft (about 672 m); the register gives 2,139 ft (652 m). The record keeps the register's figure.

The register says general visits must be arranged because the site is private property; the land trust says the preserve has been open for hiking since September 2018. The summit trail is public, but the tower itself is not a walk-in visit.

notes_for_editor: Record elevation_m 652 uses the register's 2,139 ft; the land trust and 2019 Press Democrat say 2,204 ft (about 672 m), so the record may want updating. The 1967 built year is for the Red Oat Mountain tower; the 1981 move was missing from the record and is added to events. Could not confirm from pages read whether the new steel building has opened, so status is left as the record has it (standing). Staffing as_of is undated because the group's pages carry no dates. Staffing and closure dates conflict between the 2018 volunteer report and the 2019 Press Democrat. Not used: a Cazadero CSD update that said the lookout was open, seen only in a search snippet and not read on the page.
